implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: Treat any successfully parsed JSON value that is not a list (object, number, string, boolean, null) as ERROR, using a single isinstance(value, list) check rather than enumerating rejected types
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec names 'a JSON object, a bare number, invalid JSON' as examples, not an exhaustive list; the contract says input must be a JSON array, so the positive check is the faithful reading and it also covers JSON null and top-level strings, which the spec never enumerates.

unresolved_intent.decision: A JSON boolean element is rejected as a non-string event via isinstance(event, str), which excludes bool because bool subclasses int and not str
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec says 'a non-string element' is an error but does not call out Python's bool/int aliasing; the str check is the only one where the aliasing quirk cannot produce a false accept, so no extra bool guard was added.

unresolved_intent.decision: Validate each element during the left-to-right fold and return ERROR at the first bad element, rather than pre-validating the whole array before folding
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec makes the two indistinguishable — the machine emits no per-step output and the only observable is the single final line — so the fold-and-fail-fast form was chosen because it keeps one traversal and one place where the totality invariant is enforced.

unresolved_intent.decision: Read all of stdin and hand the raw text to json.loads, which tolerates surrounding whitespace and trailing newlines; extra non-whitespace trailing content makes json.loads raise and yields ERROR
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec says 'reads one JSON value from standard input' without defining framing, empty input, or trailing bytes; delegating framing to json.loads makes the accepted set exactly 'one well-formed JSON value' and turns empty input into ERROR, which matches 'invalid JSON'.

unresolved_intent.decision: ERROR is signalled only on stdout with exit status 0; nothing is written to stderr and no non-zero exit is used for any rejection
unresolved_intent.rationale: The contract says 'print the final state name to standard output and exit 0' and 'print exactly ERROR' without granting a separate error channel; keeping exit 0 universal means the harness reads one stream and cannot see a traceback as a distinct failure mode.

compilation_report.constraint_handling: r2: second blind run of the same model on the same canonical package (ADR-027 intra-model variance)
